papers.abstract: We study the radius of absolute monotonicity of rational approximations to the exponential of the form \[ ϕ(z)=\frac{P(z)}{(1-z/b)^s}, \qquad b>0,\qquad °P\le s, \] with approximation orders two and three. For second-order approximation, we prove that the maximal radius in degree $s=5$ is $10$ and determine the unique extremizer. Hence the conjectured value $2s$ by Lóczi and Ketcheson (LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics, 17 (2014), no.~1, 159--205) remains valid in this case. In contrast, for every integer $s\ge6$ we construct explicitly a rational function with rational coefficients and exact radius \[ 2s+\frac{4(s-3)}{s^2-3s+4}>2s. \] For third-order approximation, we construct, for every $s\ge5$, an explicit rational family with exact radius \[ 2s-1>s-1+\sqrt{s^2-1}. \] These constructions disprove the conjectures of Lóczi and Ketcheson concerning rational functions with a single repeated pole.
papers.title: Maximal Absolute Monotonicity of Balanced Rational Functions with a Single Repeated Pole

papers.abstract: The public release of the complete adult fruit-fly brain connectome enables brain-scale spiking-network studies, motivating closed-loop assessment of connection loss. We test a connectome-derived controller in synthetic pursuit-escape and check record consistency. Across 576 test episodes in paired campaigns, the baseline mapping at 50% connection-row deletion yields 11/48 proportional and 0/48 relay collisions by 1 s, despite paired P/R trigger/burst schedules. The prespecified secondary relay-minus-proportional net-loss difference is -22.9 percentage points (95% seed-cluster CI [-33.3, -12.5]). Two separately recalibrated mappings yield smaller, uncertain point estimates; unequal healthy clearance, recalibration and different test cohorts limit attribution. A frozen command-rate warning detects only 2/13 baseline collisions across all tested deletion levels. In a separate author-designed fly/delayed-tank catalogue, checks plus model-specific replay detect 81/87 corruptions versus 36/87 for trusted headers, accepting all 20 distinct valid inputs (six misses). These results quantify finite-horizon collisions and the gains and limits of record checks.
papers.title: From Connection Loss to Collision: Closed-Loop Fault Assessment of a Fly-Connectome SNN

papers.abstract: Automated testing of mobile applications remains challenging when realistic user interactions must be reproduced and GUI behavior verified without relying on invasive mechanisms such as instrumentation or ADB-level control. Existing approaches, including DLD and R-DLD, detect data loss triggered by activity restarts but still depend on system-level access, which limits their applicability on real devices. This doctoral research proposes RFNIT, a multi-modal, fully non-invasive robotic framework for physical GUI interaction testing on smartphones. RFNIT supports end-to-end automation by perceiving the device state through external sensing and executing physical interactions, enabling human-like actions while preserving reproducibility and execution accuracy. The framework integrates a vision-based perception module, an LLM-driven reasoning agent, and a robotic actuator capable of performing touch, swipe, and typing gestures. Multimodal data, including external camera images and OCR-extracted text, are combined to identify GUI elements and guide subsequent testing decisions. Preliminary results indicate that RFNIT accurately recognizes buttons, text fields, and virtual keyboards from external camera input, achieving over 85\% visual detection accuracy. Ongoing and future work will focus on improving robustness, repeatability, and coverage of GUI states during long-running testing sessions.
papers.title: A Multi-Modal Robotic Framework for Physical GUI Interaction Testing

papers.abstract: This article presents web-based applets designed primarily to educate future mathematics teachers in the field of numerical algorithms and, secondarily, to serve high school students themselves. The applets allow users to explore the behaviour of basic numerical algorithms as applied to fundamental mathematical topics taught at high schools. The advantage is that no software is required, and students can intuitively test how a given method works by adjusting specific problem parameters, not only by viewing a list of approximate solutions, but especially through graphical output. Furthermore, they have access to multiple different methods for comparison.
papers.title: Support in the domain of numerical algorithms in the education of future secondary school mathematics teachers

papers.abstract: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.
papers.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice

papers.abstract: Accurate, robust, and adaptive localization is essential for various robotic operations. This paper proposes a parametric message passing (MP) algorithm for distributed collaborative localization, unifying Gaussian belief propagation (GBP) for robot state estimation and mean-field (MF) approximation for noise inference. Unlike conventional MP algorithms, the proposed formulation directly optimizes the natural parameters of beliefs, establishing a principled connection between MP and gradient estimators for handling non-conjugate terms arising from nonlinear measurement models. Beyond linearization and sampling, we further design a normalizing flow (NF)-based gradient estimator, enabling learnable sampling. End-to-end training tunes NF parameters according to the behavior of MP, improving estimation accuracy while reducing the required number of iterations. To support robot states involving rotations, the method is extended to Lie group spaces. Finally, the method is applied to a multirobot localization task fusing odometry, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) measurements, and inter-robot ultra wideband (UWB) ranging. Extensive simulations and experiments on autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) demonstrate superior state estimation accuracy, enhanced robustness and adaptability under ranging outliers and varying noise statistics, as well as good generalization across different operating conditions.
papers.title: Normalizing Flow-Enhanced Message Passing for Multirobot Collaborative Localization

papers.abstract: When annotators disagree on a label, the disagreement itself carries signal - and the number of annotators needed to capture it depends on the evaluation metric. We fine-tune NLI models on label distributions subsampled from ChaosNLI, a dataset providing 100 independent annotator judgments per item, and identify metric-dependent saturation. In our 3-class NLI setting, entropy correlation - whether the model identifies which items elicit disagreement - requires N ~ 20-50 annotators to converge, while distributional match (KL divergence) saturates by N ~ 10 (87-95% of improvement across five model seeds); the specific thresholds are estimates for this setting, and it is the phenomenon, not the constants, that we expect to generalize. This finding rests on a prior observation: soft labels carry item-specific signal that label smoothing cannot replicate. Across five smoothing intensities, entropy correlation clusters at r ~ 0.45-0.49, while soft labels reach r = 0.643 (p < 0.001); per-item analysis traces this gap to smoothing's inability to distinguish ambiguous items from clear ones. The soft label advantage replicates across two architectures (DeBERTa, RoBERTa) and a non-NLI-pretrained baseline; differential saturation additionally appears in an exploratory cross-domain evaluation on content safety. These results suggest that annotation budgets should be informed by the target evaluation metric rather than set uniformly.
papers.title: Metric-Dependent Annotation Saturation for Learning from Label Distributions

papers.abstract: Continuous Attractor Neural Networks (CANNs) traditionally rely on pre-wired recurrent connectivity to model spatial representations, path integration, and anticipatory dynamics. However, the biological mechanisms through which this structured connectivity emerges via learning remain relatively unexplored. This work presents a theoretical framework revealing how continuous attractor connectivity and its computational properties self-organize through Hebbian plasticity, firing-rate adaptation, and global inhibition. We show that translationally invariant inputs naturally drive the emergence of stable, Gaussian-profiled feedforward weights. Crucially, anticipatory dynamics arise spontaneously within these feedforward architectures, shifting the activity bump forward without requiring recurrent excitatory collaterals. This predictive shift can be linearly amplified across multilayer networks, consistent with anticipatory activity observed in the superficial layers of the entorhinal cortex. Furthermore, introducing recurrent interactions allows the network to learn connections capable of self-sustaining a moving bump of activity. Finally, by modulating the network with an external, time-varying baseline current that encodes speed, the system adjusts its intrinsic velocity to function as a precise unidirectional path integrator. Ultimately, this study suggests that prospective coding and path integration are not manually engineered features, but rather naturally co-emergent properties of a single self-organizing competitive network.
papers.title: Prospective Coding and Path Integration Emerge as Equilibrium Solutions of Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Firing-Rate Adaptation

papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.
papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles

papers.abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional (3D) formation and evolution of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) shock waves and their role in plasma heating within a solar bipolar active region. Using 3D compressible, resistive MHD simulations, we model the emergence of magnetic flux from the convection zone into a magnetized corona. Our results reveal that initial plasmoid ejections launch hot plasma jets preceded by slow-mode shocks. Unlike established 2D models, these ejections originate from multiple sites along the emerging field's periphery, resulting in shocks with a complex, inverted-U 3D morphology. Beneath these fronts, the heated plasma forms flattened, sheet-like columns. Furthermore, we find that sustained gas pressure gradients, driven by dense plasma accumulation from plasmoids, power a cool, dense upflow adjacent to the main reconnection jet. During the main reconnection phase, the collision of ejected plasmoids with the ambient field triggers the formation of fast-mode termination shocks. By mapping viscous heating directly onto these irregular 3D shock surfaces, we demonstrate that energy dissipation is highly localized. This finding provides a physical link between shock-induced viscous heating and the observed temperature enhancements at the apex of post-flare loops.
papers.title: Three-dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Shocks and Associated Plasma Heating in the Solar Atmosphere

papers.abstract: Electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational-wave (GW) sources probe the properties, environments, and evolution of compact-object mergers. S251112cm belongs to an emerging class of GW candidates with possible subsolar-mass components. We present an optical counterpart search for S251112cm with the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). Observations began 20.2 hr after the GW trigger and lasted three nights, covering approximately 780 deg$^2$ and 51% of the localization probability in the updated skymap. Our search for newly emerging, rapidly evolving, off-nuclear optical transients yielded four candidates with host-galaxy distances broadly consistent with the GW distance estimate. All four evolve substantially more slowly than AT 2017gfo, ruling out an AT 2017gfo-like origin and disfavoring their association with S251112cm as rapidly evolving kilonova counterparts. Combining WFST and DECam increases the localization probability coverage to approximately 67%. Assuming the counterpart lies within this footprint, we constrain a grid of binary-neutron-star kilonova models. For viewing angles $θ_{\rm obs}<60^\circ$, with other parameters fixed to the AT 2017gfo best-fit values, models with dynamical ejecta mass $M_{\rm dyn}\gtrsim0.01 M_\odot$ or wind ejecta mass $M_{\rm wind}\gtrsim0.05 M_\odot$ are disfavored over most of the covered GW probability. Our phenomenological analysis further constrains rapidly evolving optical transients with $T_{\rm rise,1/2}\leq2$ days to peak absolute magnitudes fainter than approximately -13 mag. To our knowledge, WFST provides the strongest optical constraints to date in the northern sky on possible rapidly evolving counterparts to this new class of GW candidates with subsolar-mass components. The comparable depths and complementary sky coverage of WFST and DECam extend these constraints across more of the localization region at similar sensitivity.
papers.title: WFST Follow-up of S251112cm: Searching for an Optical Counterpart to a Subsolar-mass Compact-binary Merger Candidate

papers.abstract: For every overlap $m\geq 3$ and every pattern length $K\geq 2m+1$, we construct an explicit permutation $p\in\mathfrak{S}_K$ such that the number of permutations containing $j$ prescribed occurrences of $p$, with successive starts separated by $K-m$, is $(2j-1)!!$ for every $j\geq 1$. Additional occurrences are permitted. We prove that the corresponding occurrence poset is the ordinal sum of a chain on $m+j(K-m-2)$ elements and a comb on $2j$ elements. An insertion bijection counts the linear extensions of the comb. This gives the uniform representatives requested in the double-factorial part of Question 6 in Section 7 of Blitvić, Kammoun and Steingrímsson, arXiv:2610.29846v1. A Lean 4 formalization and its recorded verification data accompany the paper.
papers.title: A uniform double-factorial construction for consecutive-pattern packings

papers.abstract: Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium-tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni-Ge-Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15~nm)/Ge$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$/Ge/Gd$_2$O$_3$/Si(111) heterostructures ($x = 0.08$ and $0.10$) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973~K for 10~s using X-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573~K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge$_{0.92}$Sn$_{0.08}$, whereas Ge$_{0.90}$Sn$_{0.10}$ exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973~K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni-Ge-Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573~K samples, whereas annealing at 973~K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated $M(H)$ loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.
papers.title: Investigation of the Microstructural and Magnetic Properties of Ni on GeSn Layers

papers.abstract: Pure pursuit and its variants are widely used for mobile robot path tracking owing to their simplicity and computational efficiency. However, many conventional approaches do not explicitly account for velocity and acceleration constraints, resulting in discrepancies between commanded and actual velocities that result in overshoot and degraded tracking performance. To address this problem, this paper proposes dynamic window pure pursuit (DWPP), which fundamentally reformulates the command velocity computation process to explicitly incorporate velocity and acceleration constraints. Specifically, DWPP formulates command velocity computation in the velocity space (the $v$-$ω$ plane) and selects the command velocity as the point within the dynamic window that is closest to the line $ω= κv$. Experimental results demonstrate that DWPP avoids constraint-violating commands and achieves superior path-tracking accuracy compared with conventional pure pursuit methods. The proposed method has been integrated into the official Nav2 repository and is publicly available (https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2).
papers.title: DWPP: Dynamic Window Pure Pursuit Considering Velocity and Acceleration Constraints

papers.abstract: Semi-analytic models of black-hole movies require both an emitting flow prescription and a time-dependent source variability. Existing prescriptions are often limited to either equatorial emission or time-independent sources. In this work we present a unified model for these two ingredients. First, we prescribe an off-equatorial, nongeodesic Kerr fluid rotation law by lifting an equatorial specific-angular-momentum profile to cylindrical surfaces, setting the polar component of the four-velocity to zero, normalizing the flow with the full Kerr metric at the spacetime point, and retaining the option to recover a geodesic-like plunging prescription when needed. Second, we use this velocity as the disk advection field in a four-dimensional inhomogeneous, anisotropic Matérn-like Gaussian random field. We provide a parametrized model for a torus-like disk and a central jet through a single composite correlation tensor. The resulting effective model is an implementation-ready prescription for time-dependent thick-disk and disk-jet emission for relativistic studies.
papers.title: A Four-Dimensional Gaussian Random Field Generator for Modeling Spatiotemporal Variability in Astrophysical Sources

papers.abstract: Alexander Lerchner's recent work on the 'abstraction fallacy' argues that computational functionalism confuses physical processes with abstract descriptions, and that symbolic computation alone cannot instantiate consciousness. Yet these claims were anticipated by Korzybski's map-territory distinction, Searle's critique of strong artificial intelligence, Floridi's levels of abstraction, Spencer et al.'s observer-relativity arguments, Winograd and Flores's account of computation as socially grounded practice, and Nasuto and Bishop's biological arguments. Synthesizing these contributions, this paper advances a form of non-computational physicalism: consciousness depends upon intrinsically organized, metabolically grounded physical dynamics rather than abstract computation, whilst leaving open the possibility of artificial consciousness. An objection is that this critique targets an outdated computationalism. Mechanistic computationalism, associated with Milkowski, Piccinini, Craver, Bechtel, and Kaplan, treats computation as a property of physically realized mechanisms rather than substrate-independent formalism. Although this represents an important advance, it does not dissolve the abstraction fallacy. Computational attributions remain dependent upon choices of state individuation, system boundaries, and interpretive mapping that are not determined by physical facts alone. Kaplan and Craver's 'model-to-mechanism mapping' constrains computational descriptions without eliminating their dependence upon an external observer. Grounding computation in neural mechanisms does not confer intrinsic significance or the normativity explored by Bickhard and Nasuto and Bishop. The abstraction fallacy persists wherever computational descriptions are treated as constitutive of, rather than descriptive of, physical reality.
papers.title: From Maps to Metabolism: Historical Precedents and a Unified Critique of Computationalism

papers.abstract: White's illusion is a striking demonstration of context-dependent brightness and lightness perception. In earlier work, we developed a forward translucency-based formula capable of producing approximately constant perceived appearance across varying backgrounds. While validating that formulation, we observed a notable population-level pattern: individuals selected slightly different correction percentages for "constant perception," while the population average remained remarkably stable across experiments. In this paper, we propose an evolutionary hypothesis for this phenomenon. We suggest that a simple constant-percentage correction function could have emerged as an adaptive mechanism for maintaining useful material and reflectance judgments under variable illumination. Under this interpretation, the stability of the population mean may reflect a conserved perceptual mechanism, whereas individual differences may reflect learning, adaptation, or variation around a shared computational response. Using a modification of our previously published forward model, we show that White's illusion can be reproduced by applying a constant-percentage correction to background luminance. The model therefore provides a compact computational account of the observed population-level regularity and motivates a testable evolutionary interpretation of individual variation in contextual lightness judgments.
papers.title: An Evolutionary Hypothesis for White's Illusion: Constant Percentage Correction and Modern Individual Variation

papers.abstract: String compactifications and runaway-dilaton models can contain light scalar directions. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. Its gauge kinetic functions, matter-metric or Yukawa slopes, source charge, scalar trajectory, and scalar range determine a Damour--Donoghue weak-equivalence-principle (WEP) vector and a clock-drift vector. The fit assumes one long-range scalar or an aligned multi-field direction. With that assumption, WEP tests and secular clock drifts probe related projections of the same scalar-slope vector. The minimal two-charge Damour--Donoghue fit uses Ti--Pt MICROSCOPE, Be--Ti torsion-balance, and $^{85}$Rb--$^{87}$Rb atom-interferometer data, then adds the Yb$^+$ E3/E2 secular $α$-drift row. The WEP-only fit gives $D_{\hat m}=(-6.06\pm34.91)\times10^{-12}$ and $D_e=(8.80\pm46.46)\times10^{-12}$, with correlation $-0.99958$. The clock input is $\dotα/α=1.0(1.1)\times10^{-18}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. It matches the WEP marginal reach when $|ζ|=2.37\times10^{-8}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, with $ζ=\dotφ/α_E$. For the benchmark $\dotφ=ξH_0$ and $α_E=10^{-3}α_0$, this gives $ξ/α_0\simeq0.34$. A model becomes testable after it supplies $r=D_{\hat m}/D_e$, the scalar amplitude, and $ζ$. The Damour--Piazza--Veneziano runaway-dilaton estimate lies near $η\sim10^{-12}$ for order-unity $n=2$ parameters, well above the MICROSCOPE-level WEP scale. In the representative-isotope two-charge model, a MICROSCOPE-level Be--Ti-like row would reduce the long WEP axis by a factor $27.8$; a repeated Ti--Pt-like row would barely change it. The calculation tests compactification-level predictions for string-derived dilaton or modulus sectors after the model supplies its low-energy data.
papers.title: Clock--WEP Tests of String-Derived Dilaton and Modulus Sectors

papers.abstract: Massive moons around rocky exoplanets are expected outcomes of giant impacts, yet no exomoon has been securely confirmed. We address this problem using meshless finite-mass simulations of giant impacts between differentiated rocky planets that include stellar tidal and Coriolis forces in a local co-rotating frame for orbital periods of 1--300 days, and compare these simulations with otherwise identical collisions in isolation. We find that stellar perturbations impose a severe formation-stage bottleneck on moon-forming disks. Ultra-short-period impacts leave essentially no surviving circumplanetary disk, whereas 10-day systems retain only strongly depleted, radially truncated, and dynamically compact disks. High impact velocities, expected for close-in planets, are devastating for disk generation, while retrograde impacts can slightly compensate for disk mass depletion. These results show that stellar perturbations can suppress exomoon formation around close-in rocky planets, reshaping expectations for the demographics of exomoons.
papers.title: A Formation-Stage Bottleneck for Exomoons around Close-in Rocky Planets

papers.abstract: We have investigated the effects of Lorentz violation (LV) on the bright ring in Sgr A* images illuminated by the 230 GHz thermal synchrotron emission from radiatively inefficient accretion flows around a rotating LV black hole within the low-energy Hořava gravity framework. Our results reveal that the LV parameter reduces the bright ring diameter yet increases its width, luminosity, azimuthal asymmetry and orientation angle. A higher spin parameter strengthens the LV-induced effects on the bright ring properties. Increasing disk thickness reduces the ring diameter and enhances the LV parameter's effects on this diameter. The ring width shows no systematic dependence on the disk thickness. These quantities of the bright ring display similar trends against the black hole spin and the LV parameter for the rotating LV black hole. Using EHT observational data of Sgr A*, we find that, at fixed disk thickness, the parameter-space map illustrates that the bounded range of the LV parameter first broadens and then contracts with the growing black hole spin, and shifts toward smaller LV parameter values. In addition, the LV parameter narrows the bounded range of black hole spin: negative LV parameter values shift this range to a higher spin, while positive values shift it to a lower spin. Finally, we probe effects of the LV parameter on the peak position value and the width of the primary image and the $n=1$ photon ring for the rotating LV black hole. The peak positions and their widths nearly always decrease with the LV parameter. The peak position differences for various LV parameters are more pronounced for a purely Keplerian accretion flow. In addition, the primary image and the $n=1$ photon ring produced by purely radially free-falling flows are broader than their counterparts generated by purely Keplerian flows.
papers.title: Signatures of Lorentz violation in the bright ring for Sgr A* images from radiatively inefficient accretion flows

papers.abstract: We predict the spin thermal Hall effect in nonreciprocal magneto-optical many-body systems, in which a longitudinal radiative heat current generates a transverse accumulation of the spin angular momentum carried by thermal photons. We show that this effect and the inverse spin thermal Hall effect constitute an Onsager-Casimir reciprocal pair, thereby establishing heat and photon spin as coupled transport channels in nonreciprocal photonic systems. The second law of thermodynamics imposes fundamental bounds on the spin-heat coupling, leading to a thermal-spin figure of merit that quantifies the efficiency of radiative spin-heat conversion. Our results establish a complete thermodynamic framework for photon spin caloritronics and lay the conceptual foundations for spin-controlled thermal radiation and nonreciprocal photonic thermal devices.
papers.title: Radiative spin caloritronics in nonreciprocal many-body systems

papers.abstract: The magnetic field topology undergoes a drastic transition near the separatrix in magnetic confinement fusion devices, inducing topological chaos. This phenomenon is investigated across tokamaks, stellarators, and the RFX-mod reversed-field pinch. Within this boundary region, self-optimized fluxes of shear-generated magnetic and cross-helicity, together with the ensemble-averaged magnetic moment, are hypothesized to govern plasma stability, self-organization, and transport. By treating the averaged magnetic moment as an active scalar and using the Fokker-Planck equation to reconcile kinetic and fluid descriptions, this study couples its dynamics with a novel multichannel, self-optimized helicity cascade loop. The derived spectral laws for the floating potential and ion saturation current agree with measurements from numerous experiments. Distributed chaos theory quantifies the randomness of the observed states, revealing that a narrow layer at the separatrix suppresses strong core randomness, transforming it into distributed chaos in the scrape-off layer. A constrained variational principle for active control has also been considered. Tuning Lagrangian multipliers via helicity injection drives the system toward an attractor state that stabilizes the separatrix shear layer, suppresses edge-localized modes, and spreads the heat load, using magnetic reconnection as a nonlinear solver. This framework circumvents conventional diffusive limitations, providing an analytical foundation to model heat-load patterns and stochastic ripple loss in next-step devices.
papers.title: Edge turbulence controlled by topologically self-optimized fluxes in fusion devices

papers.abstract: We derive a quantum speed limit for ergotropy charging in the $N$-qubit Dicke battery. With the qubits initially in their ground state and the charger in a coherent state of mean photon number $\bar{n}$, the charging time to a target fraction $\varepsilon$ of the maximum extractable work obeys, in the classical-field limit, $Γ_N τ^{*}(\varepsilon) \geq \arcsin\sqrt{\varepsilon}$, where $Γ_N = 2λ\sqrt{\bar{n}/N}$ is a single rate combining the light-matter coupling, the charger amplitude and the system size. The bound is geometric: although the ergotropy is defined by an optimisation over unitaries, it reduces to a fixed function of the angle swept by the collective spin on the Bloch sphere, and the drive bounds the rate at which that angle can grow, so the charging time is at least the required arc divided by the maximum angular velocity. The reduction rests on an exact statement about work extraction: only the coherent component of the drive delivers extractable work, while its vacuum fluctuations deposit energy that remains locked in the passive state. This makes the short-time coefficient independent of the charger occupation, and it is what separates a bound on extractable work from a bound on stored energy, which no instantaneous-power argument can supply. At finite charger occupation the inequality is tested rather than proved: numerical integration of the full Dicke Hamiltonian, with a dynamical charger and a mixed battery state, finds the bound respected at every admitted charging time for two to five qubits, and approached most closely in the limit of small target work. The familiar square-root estimate is the chord to this arc, recovered in the small-angle limit and weaker whenever a large fraction of the maximum work is required.
papers.title: Tight Quantum Speed Limit for Ergotropy Charging in the N-Qubit Dicke Battery

papers.abstract: Quadratic $f(R)$ gravity carries a massive scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, whose finite range $λ$ screens its influence on the geometry outside a compact object. We show that this screening severs the exterior of a black hole from that of a neutron star of the same mass. Correction to the Schwarzschild metric is Yukawa-suppressed, falling as $e^{-r/λ}$ in the coupling, and is thus invisible to any expansion in powers of that coupling; the exterior is moreover intrinsically isotropic, so that inverting the temporal potential alone, as one does for single-potential solutions, fails to solve the field equations. Applying the Gibbons & Werner method of the Gauss-Bonnet theorem to this geometry, we find the leading deflection angle to be exactly the general-relativistic, ($b$: impact parameter), scalaron contributions cancelling identically in the combination that bends light. First correction carries the unfamiliar signature $λ^{-1/2}b^{-3/2}e^{-b/λ}$, screened beyond the scalaron range and confirmed against direct quadrature to around 20% at $b=4λ$, improving to 7% at $b=12λ$. What survives is the ingredients that deliver it, namely, non-analyticity in the coupling, the intrinsically isotropic gauge, the closed-form screened correction and the pressure-weighted scalar charge, are obtained within a single, self-consistent derivation here. A static black hole carries no scalar hair, and lenses precisely as general relativity requires; a neutron star acquires a scalar charge weighted by the pressure supporting it against collapse, and does not. Weak lensing therefore closes as a discriminant of the theory, whilst the horizon, as against a material surface, remains one in principle. The observational advantage lies in the strong-field imaging of the photon sphere, and in the stellar interior, where the scalar charge is fixed by the equation of state.
papers.title: Screened Scalar Hair and the Weak-Lensing Separation of Black Holes from Neutron Stars in Quadratic $f(R)$ Gravity

papers.abstract: In multimodal multi-hop question answering, we focus on the initial retrieval stage via two distinct tasks: (1) evidence set completion, retrieving missing evidence given context, and (2) sequential pool construction, iteratively building the top-$K$ pool from the scratch. Under these settings, we point out that conventional iterative retrieval frameworks often suffer from Semantic Anchoring, where previously fetched evidence traps the retriever and yields entity-centric redundancy. To break this trap, we propose GRAIL (Gap-aware Retrieval via Adaptive Implicit Localization), a paradigm that performs implicit query rewriting directly at the embedding level. By context-subtractive query steering, GRAIL excels at compositional cross-modal reasoning, while additive embedding updates show strength on localized information aggregation. To leverage these complementary strengths, we propose a Task-Adaptive Hybrid Framework, achieving a 35.7% macro-averaged performance gain on the MultimodalQA evidence set completion task. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that sequential GRAIL retrieves in a superior, noise-resilient manner, significantly expanding the search horizon through iterative gap-aware optimization.
papers.title: Subtraction Gets You More: Gap-Aware Retrieval for Multimodal Multi-Hop QA

papers.abstract: A growing number of transiting exoplanets exhibit spectroscopic evidence that their leading and trailing limbs differ. Interpreting these observations is now the limiting step. The standard approach of fitting limb-resolved transit depths results in highly anti-correlated transit depths, and treating them as independent measurements can result in strongly biased ($3σ$) retrieved molecular abundances. We present an inference framework that avoids these correlations by using the temporal signature of limb asymmetry instead. This wavelength-dependent shift in mid-transit time, or `time-shift spectrum', carries the limb-asymmetry information, is measurable from existing light curves with a spherically symmetric transit model, and is uncorrelated with the spherically-averaged transit depth. Simultaneously fitting the resulting transmission and time-shift spectrum with an independent atmospheric column for each limb enables the retrieval of limb-resolved properties from two independent measurements. We demonstrate that this approach reduces the mean squared error on the retrieved molecular abundances by factors of $\sim30-50$ relative to next best of the alternative approaches currently adopted in the field, and improves retrieved abundance precision by $\sim3-6\times$. We apply the framework to WASP-94A b and present its panchromatic limb-resolved spectrum, spanning 0.8-5~$μ$m and combining NIRISS/SOSS and NIRSpec/G395H observations. The planet's morning limb remains aerosol-obscured across this entire range, while its evening limb constrains the abundances of H$_2$O, CO$_2$, CO, and H$_2$S. We measure a limb-to-limb temperature difference of $415\pm58$~K at 1~mbar. This limb-resolved analysis finds [M/H]=+0.32$^{+0.11}_{-0.11}$ and C/O=0.724$^{+0.013}_{-0.013}$, consistent with the host star.
papers.title: A New Method for Constraining 3D Exoplanet Atmospheres: Application to WASP-94A b's Panchromatic Spectrum

papers.abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. To test this hypothesis, we performed simulations of the combined stellar, tidal, and atmospheric evolution and confirmed that TOI-2257 b does lie near this boundary, regardless of whether it formed with or without a primordial hydrogen envelope. In the mini-Neptune scenario, we find that all cases retain an envelope of at least 0.02 M$_\oplus$ for 8 Gyr, but that the envelope mass can be halved if it was initially larger than 0.2 M$_\oplus$. We find that tidal evolution only occurs for cases with initial envelope masses larger than 0.02 M$_\oplus$ because their radii are large enough to generate significant torques. In the super-Earth scenario, the planet could lose $\sim$10 Earth ocean masses of surface water during the $\sim$75 Myr pre-main sequence and therefore could be habitable if it formed with $\gtrsim$2x Earth's surface water mass. The predicted tidal heating surface flux tends to be similar to Io, with no cases approaching the flux required to drive a runaway greenhouse. We find that if the planet is rocky, then eccentricities larger than 0.62 today are strongly disfavored, implying that larger eccentricities could confirm the gaseous nature of the planet. These results suggest that TOI-2257 b could provide valuable constraints on mini-Neptune properties and new insight into the radius valley shape as a function of eccentricity.
papers.title: The Limits of Tidal Circularization and Atmospheric Escape for Mini-Neptunes and Super-Earths: The Case of TOI-2257 b

papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel regularization design to effectively smooth policy functions in reinforcement learning. While regularization that enhances ``global'' Lipschitz continuity was initially considered, it has been limited to ``local'' Lipschitz continuity due to a tradeoff between smoothness and expressiveness. However, it has become apparent that the original implementation is cumbersome and does not provide sufficient smoothing, leading to a preference for simpler implementations. This stems from a discrepancy between theory and implementation, and a more appropriate implementation can expect to facilitate smoothing. Therefore, this paper identifies three reasons why the original implementation does not function adequately and provides remedies for them. This modified regularization performs well across multiple tasks and algorithms, successfully achieving smooth motion with sufficient control performance. Furthermore, by applying it to sim-to-real reinforcement learning for a quadruped robot, it is demonstrated that smooth and energy-efficient motion provides robustness against sudden changes in target velocity commands.
papers.title: Redesigning Regularization for Effective Policy Smoothing

papers.abstract: We develop a theoretical description of quantum wave mixing (QWM) in a cascaded waveguide-QED system of two superconducting qubits, where the probe is driven by an external coherent tone and by the resonance fluorescence of a strongly driven source qubit. Starting from the field correlation functions of the source emission, we derive an effective master-equation treatment for the probe and identify the regime in which the incident fluorescence is characterized by anomalous correlations. When the coherent Rayleigh component of the source spectrum is suppressed, the probe equations of motion become equivalent to those for a qubit driven by a coherent tone and broadband squeezed light, although the ligt emitted by the source is non-Gaussian and antibunched. This equivalence implies a selection rule for the peaks of the QWM spectrum, with a strong suppression of sidebands associated with processes involving an odd number of photons taken from the source field. Numerical simulations of the full cascaded two-qubit model for different ratios of radiative decay rates unambiguously confirm the participation of correlated photon pairs in QWM processes. The current research illustrates that the analysis of peak amplitudes can be used to probe photon statistics in the incident nonclassical field.
papers.title: Photon pairs, squeezed light and the quantum wave mixing effect in a cascaded qubit system

papers.abstract: In this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of magnetically charged Euler--Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes in the extended phase space. We classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the EH coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. For negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a Van der Waals-like small/large black-hole transition. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated QNM trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. The GHS limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.
papers.title: Phase transitions and quasinormal modes of Euler-Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes

papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made substantial progress in multilingual question answering, yet their ability to understand low-resource sociolinguistic contexts remains under-explored. We study North Korea as a unique testbed where decades of division have produced distinct differences from South Korea in vocabulary, orthography, norms, and ideological discourse. We introduce LENS (Language and sociocultural Evaluation for North Korean Society), a human-validated benchmark of 1,765 questions evaluating LLMs across three dimensions: linguistic robustness, sociocultural perspective alignment, and domain-specific knowledge. Evaluating diverse recent LLMs, we find a modest performance drop on North Korean language inputs, a larger gap in sociocultural perspective alignment, and severe limitations on domain-specific knowledge. Qualitative analysis reveals that models often conflate formal institutions with lived realities, project liberal-democratic assumptions, or rely on coarse stereotypes. Our results demonstrate that linguistic similarity alone does not guarantee sociocultural or domain-specific understanding, highlighting the critical need for grounded evaluation resources for underrepresented cultural and political contexts.
papers.title: North or South? Diagnosing LLMs' Understanding of North Korean Language, Society, and Knowledge

papers.abstract: We present the scattering modes of the oscillon, to the first three orders in the Fodor expansion, in terms of elementary functions. In the case of relativistic modes, these results are new. We use them to fully decompose the field and also to analytically invert the decomposition. In quantum field theory, this allows us to show that the corresponding creation and annihilation operators satisfy the usual oscillator algebra, extending to relativistic modes the demonstration that, at a fixed order in the Fodor expansion, a periodic oscillon state exists.
papers.title: Oscillon Floquet Modes and the Operators that Excite Them

papers.abstract: Reusing evaluator-derived step rewards across evaluation channels raises a measurement question: does the assigned direction remain stable? We define Agent Step Value (ASV) as a channel-indexed before/after target-margin gain and identify the state-by-channel interaction from a matched 2x2 design. Across frozen PubMed question-answering transitions, cross-channel gain signs disagree on 48.3% of comparisons, compared with 0.3% for same-channel retries. Transition interactions are nearly balanced in sign (median +0.014; 10% trimmed mean -0.033), but asymmetric negative magnitudes produce a positive direct mean and a negative generated-view mean under the empirical target mixture. Equal-target weighting preserves a negative mean interaction but not this strict mean reversal. Matched retrieval designs localize the negative component to the generated-view coordinate and retain its direction across three sign checks that vary readout and evaluator stack. In a matched 512-token source-contract follow-up, source-only generation restores the positive mean direction on artifact-bearing retrievals and removes parser-detected support claims from artifact-free before-state views. These results support an explanation in which generated support inflates the pre-retrieval baseline. The resulting audit can localize channel sensitivity and test an intervention before step rewards are reused.
papers.title: Agent Step Value: Auditing Evaluation-Channel Sensitivity in Black-Box Agent Traces

papers.abstract: Event ontology is the foundational framework for defining events in a dataset. Event type induction generally involves domain experts who define guidelines for creating event types and their names based on the dataset's domain and scope. However, this process is resource-intensive in terms of annotation costs and is prone to human biases. To alleviate the need for manual event ontology creation, we propose the CLUE framework for event type induction, naming, and annotation. Our main contributions in this work are: 1) designing a novel joint embedding representation for expressing both the verb-centric view and the semantic view of events; 2) event type induction using contrastive loss guided clustering; 3) event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at https://github.com/PratikMaitra/CLUE.
papers.title: CLUE: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Unsupervised Event Type Induction and Annotation

papers.abstract: We characterize the gravitational radiation present in the general Plebański-Demiański type~D solution with cosmological constant $Λ$ of any sign. We show that radiation escapes towards infinity if and only if the acceleration parameter is non-zero. We calculate the Cotton-York tensor and the boundary stress-energy tensor at infinity for negative $Λ$, and for positive $Λ$ the $D$ tensor that complements initial or final data at $\mathscr{J}$. In addition, we recast a recent parametrization of this family of metrics into a new form by a simple homothety, correctly identifying $Λ$, and study the existence and regularity of the possible axes of symmetry, searching for a relation between deficit angles and radiation. We also identify the branch of general non-radiating solutions with non-vanishing Cotton-York tensor at $ \mathscr{J} $.
papers.title: Study of gravitational radiation at $\mathscr{J}$ for the general type-D Einstein-Maxwell solution with cosmological constant

papers.abstract: Searches for QCD axions with masses in the neV/$c^2$ mass range are strongly motivated by new physics at the GUT scale and by well-motivated pre-inflationary axion symmetry breaking scales. This parameter space is challenging to probe due to the small axion-photon couplings, which typically require large, high-field magnets with substantial stored energy. In this paper, we propose a new experimental geometry based on a narrow-bore, segmented solenoid that optimizes the collection of the axion-induced signal using LC resonators outside the high-field region of the magnet bore. This alternative optimization significantly reduces the required stored magnetic energy while preserving sensitivity, enabling a near-term experiment in the 30-200 MHz (120-830 neV/$c^2$) range, with a cost-effective, staged scaling to a GUT-scale experiment in the 100 kHz-30 MHz (0.4-120 neV/$c^2$) range.
papers.title: DMRadio-Core: A new approach for GUT-scale axion searches

papers.abstract: Synthetic-template subtraction is widely used to measure chromospheric activity in large spectroscopic surveys. However, many solar-like FGK stars show systematically negative Ca II infrared triplet (IRT) activity indices. We investigate this effect using solar-like stars from LAMOST DR9, MaStar, and XSL DR3, measuring activity indices (R^+) for both the Ca II H&K and IRT lines within a uniform framework. We find that observational effects contribute to the scatter but do not explain the systematic negative bias in R^+_IRT. This bias mainly arises because radiative-equilibrium photospheric models lack the chromospheric layers, which exhibit a temperature rise and provide additional Ca II IRT opacity. This additional opacity makes the observed IRT cores deeper than those in the synthetic photospheric profiles. NLTE effects may contribute but are unlikely to dominate. The different behavior of the H&K and IRT diagnostics can be related to their different source-function behavior: the stronger chromospheric source-function enhancement of H&K makes their cores more likely to appear in emission. Increasing the adopted microturbulent velocity partially mitigates the negative offset, serving as an empirical compensation for missing atmospheric physics. In addition, R^+ values derived from different synthesis configurations show systematic offsets but generally preserve strong linear correlations, indicating that they can be cross-calibrated. These results clarify the origin of negative Ca II IRT residual indices and help interpret template-dependent systematics in chromospheric activity measurements.
papers.title: Revisiting Ca II Activity Indices in FGK Stars: Systematic Biases in Infrared Triplet Measurements

papers.abstract: The world's first Compton scattering measurements on a $^3$He target were performed to probe neutron electromagnetic polarizabilities. Differential cross sections were measured at laboratory angles of $40^\circ$, $55^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $115^\circ$, $150^\circ$, using circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic photon beams at weighted mean energy values of 61.5 and 97.1 MeV from the High Intensity $γ$-ray Source at the Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory. Comparisons with chiral effective field theory show good agreement at 97.1 MeV but over-prediction at 61.5 MeV, motivating further theoretical development.
papers.title: First Measurement of Compton Scattering on $^3\text{He}$ at HI$γ$S

papers.abstract: We propose a hybrid sampling method, tensor-network population annealing (TNPA), which combines tensor-network (TN) initialization with population annealing (PA). We apply this method to the two-dimensional Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass. The approach is motivated by the limitations of existing methods: TN-based samplers can become numerically unstable in frustrated spin systems at low temperatures, whereas conventional PA requires a long annealing schedule when started from the high-temperature limit. In TNPA, TN contractions are used only within a reliable temperature range to generate initial configurations that are close to the equilibrium distribution. The subsequent low-temperature equilibration is then carried out by PA. To stabilize the initialization process, we introduce a diagnostic based on the effective sample size that adaptively selects the initialization temperature. The proposed framework provides a practical and physically motivated route to low-temperature sampling by combining the complementary strengths of TN and PA.
papers.title: Tensor-Network Population Annealing

papers.abstract: Output-only safety monitoring sees only the end of a model's computation, yet the model computes its answer before emitting it: what it is internally poised to say is safety-critical. Jacobian-space (J-space) readouts, linear maps from hidden states to the output vocabulary via the model's input-output Jacobian, have been proposed as a window on behaviorally accessible internal content, and a first safety protocol (JADR) showed that danger recognition is readable there. What remains unknown is how this accessible content relates to the latent-space safety geometry studied by representation engineering, and how safety training shapes it. We introduce two quantitative bridges: (i) a transport-amplification profile $A_\ell$, measuring how strongly a latent safety direction is carried toward output space by each layer's Jacobian, and (ii) a paired base-vs-tuned protocol that attributes accessibility to training provenance. Across four small model pairs (135M to 1.5B, three lens-fit seeds), tuned checkpoints concentrate recognition in upper-middle layers, and at 0.5B DPO installs refusal while J-space recognition drops to chance: training can widen the accessibility gap exactly where behavioral safety looks best. A deployment audit closes the loop: monitor-aware GCG-style suffixes suppress the prompt-side monitor at zero behavioral cost at every scale; only a learned monitor rung resists its own adaptive re-attack; the training-time defense fails its re-attack at every penalty weight; steering shows the amplification profile is descriptive, not causal; and continuous-prefix optimization fails where discrete search succeeds. Safety monitoring, training, and evaluation must operate on accessibility itself, not on outputs alone.
papers.title: From Latent Space to Jacobian Space: Measuring, Evading, and Training Against Safety-Content Accessibility

papers.abstract: Fermionic linear optics (FLO) with Gaussian resources is known to be efficiently classically simulable. We show that this changes for fermions with internal degrees of freedom once the circuit is equipped with mid-circuit number monitoring and classical feedforward. In our architecture, the measurement record routes the selected blocks into a fixed-order Bell-fusion pairing geometry. On the level of the classical description, the permutation sum then no longer collapses to a single determinant or Pfaffian. Each accepted branch expands as a signed sum of path-ordered products of typically non-commuting dressed blocks, and branch amplitudes are matrix elements of the resulting non-commutative trace polynomials. Numerically, we observe Porter-Thomas statistics for the conditional branch distribution and rapid growth of the minimal order-respecting matrix product operator bond dimension. Under reasonable complexity assumptions, these results identify mid-circuit measurement-induced non-commutativity as a route to sampling hardness for noninteracting fermions, with the non-Gaussianity confined to a fixed preparation-and-readout interface rather than to the coherent FLO evolution.
papers.title: Measurement-induced non-commutativity in adaptive fermionic linear optics

papers.abstract: Evaluating the occurrence and triggers of large language model (LLM) behaviors - such as sycophancy, self-preference, or over-confidence - is critical for predicting real-world model deployment risks. However, existing situated behavioral evaluations typically ignore cultural context, limiting their generalizability across an increasingly global user base. To address this gap, we propose CuBEs - Culturally-situated Behavior Evaluations that probe for response patterns across diverse user cultures. We first extend an automated testing pipeline to inject cultural context into behavioral test scenarios and subsequent evaluation. We assess the cultural adaptability of this pipeline by building a human-labeled dataset that captures nuanced dimensions of behavior understanding across 12 distinct cultures. Our dataset reveals significant cross-cultural variations that one-size-fits all judgments fail to capture. Through evaluating 13 open- and closed-source LLMs, we find that introducing cultural situatedness in the evaluation scenario creates significant variation in the presence of a behavior. For example, while our baseline experiments testing for political bias capture localized Western political dimensions like the American conservative-progressive divide, non-Western culturally situated evaluations surface entirely different axes of bias such as religious and colonial political issues. Our findings demonstrate that standard, culturally-agnostic evaluations fail to capture these shifts, highlighting the necessity of culturally situated behavioral testing for global deployments.
papers.title: CuBEs: Culturally-Situated Behavioral Evaluations and the Limitations of Culture-Blind LLM Judges

papers.abstract: Aircraft outer mould lines are often heavily constrained early by payload requirements, manufacturability limits, and low-observability considerations. The remaining aerodynamic design space is typically small, highly constrained, and difficult to represent using a concise and physically meaningful set of design variables. A structural modal parameterisation method (MPM) is introduced for such problems. The method constructs a tunable pseudo-structure and solves its eigenvalue problem to obtain a modal basis, from which a selected subset of modes parameterises the geometry. Boundary conditions, stiffness distribution, density, thickness, and added masses are treated as intentional basis-design variables that shape the admissible deformation space prior to optimisation. The resulting design coordinates are independent of any specific flow solver, making the approach broadly applicable. For tightly constrained aerodynamic shape optimisation problems, it provides a practical balance of parameter conciseness, robust constraint awareness, and geometric flexibility.
papers.title: Geometry Parameterisation via a Structural Modal Basis for Aerodynamic Shape Optimisation

papers.abstract: Precise atmospheric abundances of giant exoplanets are becoming increasingly prevalent and there is a need to systematically convert these measurements into metrics that inform us about the planets' accretion history. We present a quantitative framework for relating atmospheric composition to the accretion of metals and primordial gas. This includes i) new relations that simplify and generalize the connection between atmospheric metallicity and metal mass fraction, ii) methods for inferring the source of the metals and quantifying the quantity of metals accreted via different sources, and iii) relating the derived quantities to expectations from formation models. We also derive a new estimate of the minimum disk mass needed to form a planetary system based on the amount of excess metals accreted by a planet, assuming that this excess originates from the drift and evaporation of pebbles at condensation fronts. This paper is accompanied by an open-source code that implements the methods presented herein.
papers.title: Quantitative Links between Formation and Atmospheric Composition for Giant Planets

papers.abstract: Autoregressive generative models -- including Transformers, recurrent neural networks, classical Kalman filters, state space models, and Mamba -- all generate sequences by sampling each output from a deterministic summary of the past, producing genuinely non-Markovian observed processes. We develop a general theoretical framework based on stochastic thermodynamics for this class of architectures and introduce the entropy production, which can be efficiently estimated from sampled trajectories without exponential overhead, despite the non-Markovian nature of the observed dynamics. As a proof-of-concept experiment with a large language model (LLM), we evaluate the entropy production for a pre-trained Transformer-based model, GPT-2. We find that the token-level entropy production is dominated by a syntactic artifact, while the sentence-level entropy production tends to be larger for causally ordered than for non-causal text sets. This observation is supported by a re-evaluation with a substantially larger model, Qwen3-4B-Base. We also demonstrate the framework in the linear Gaussian case, where the model reduces to the Kalman innovation representation and the entropy production admits an analytical expression. We also show that the entropy production decomposes exactly into non-negative per-step contributions in terms of retrospective inference, and each of those terms further splits into information-theoretically meaningful terms: a compression loss and a model mismatch. Our results establish a bridge between stochastic thermodynamics and modern generative models, and provide a starting point for using irreversibility as a quantitative probe of the highly non-Markovian processes generated by models such as LLMs.
papers.title: Stochastic Thermodynamics for Autoregressive Generative Models: A Non-Markovian Perspective
